title: Characterization conjecture for arithmetic functions satisfying a quadratic-form equation
statement:
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{C}$ satisfy

$$
f(u^2+kv^2)=f(u)^2+kf(v)^2
$$

for all $u,v\in\mathbb{N}$. **Characterization conjecture.** Exactly one of the following possibilities holds: (1) $f(n)\equiv0$; (2) for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $f(n)=n$ if there exist $u,v\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $n=u^2+kv^2$, and $f(n)=\pm n$ otherwise; or (3) for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $f(n)=\frac{1}{k+1}$ if there exist $u,v\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $n=u^2+kv^2$, and $f(n)=\pm\frac{1}{k+1}$ otherwise. The conjecture extends the preceding theorem, which establishes the characterization only in the cases treated there; the general validity for all $k\in\mathbb{N}$ remains open.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.05039

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2016).
source_name: Lihua You, Yafei Chen and Pingzhi Yuan, “A characterization of arithmetic functions satisfying f(u^2+kv^2)=f^2(u)+kf^2(v)”, arXiv:1606.05039 (2016).
